title: Uyghur Khaganate
capsule: The Uyghur Khaganate (744–840) was a Turkic imperial confederation centred on the Orkhon Valley in Mongolia that replaced the Second Turkic Khaganate after the Uyghur, Basmyl, and Karluk tribes revolted against the Göktürks in 744. Under Khagan Moyanchur (r. 747–759) the Uyghurs became indispensable allies of the Tang dynasty, providing cavalry that helped suppress the An Lushan Rebellion (755–763) in exchange for massive silk payments and trade privileges. The khaganate adopted Manichaean religion under Bögü Khan after 762, a singular choice among steppe powers that shaped art, script, and court culture. In 840 the Yenisei Kyrgyz invaded, killed the last khagan, and scattered the Uyghur confederacy; surviving groups fled to found successor states in Ganzhou, Dunhuang, and Turfan.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory in the Orkhon Valley is attested by the Orkhon inscriptions and Tang annals; the full steppe periphery of khaganate suzerainty is reconstructed from tribute lists and military campaigns and remains approximate beyond the Mongolian heartland.
